findings.summary: Feature flag checked BEFORE requireSession in all three handlers (GET, POST, PATCH). Spec requires auth-first. Unauthenticated requests get 503 instead of 401, leaking feature availability to anonymous callers.

Server component MatchesPage calls getStore().getDatabase() and listMatches() with no session check and no feature flag check. Unauthenticated users navigating to /matches receive all DB matches in the rendered HTML.

parseInt(idStr, 10) result is not validated for NaN or negative values before use. PATCH /api/matches/abc passes NaN to getMatch(); PATCH /api/matches/-1 passes -1. Both hit the DB without a 400 rejection. Missing: isNaN(id) || id < 1 guard.

score field accepts NaN/Infinity: `typeof score === 'number' ? score : 0` passes NaN and Infinity through to createMatch. SQLite INTEGER column coerces these to NULL via better-sqlite3, silently storing NULL instead of rejecting the input.

parseInt on limit/offset query params is not guarded against NaN. ?limit=abc yields NaN, which passes the `limit !== undefined` check in listMatches and produces `LIMIT NaN` SQL. better-sqlite3 may throw a runtime error or silently ignore.

Action buttons for 'archived' matches are all hidden (Save/Dismiss/Archive each gated on status !== 'archived'). The transition table allows archived→saved, but the UI offers no button to trigger it. Archived matches become permanently stuck in the UI.

MATCHES_ENABLED feature flag is enforced in API routes but not in the /matches server-rendered page. When the feature is disabled, the page still renders all matches from the DB — inconsistent feature-flag enforcement.
Catch-all 500 handler returns error.message verbatim: { error: error.message }. SQLite/better-sqlite3 error messages can expose table names, column names, and constraint details to API callers.

checkAuth helper uses fragile duck-type check (presence of .session property) to discriminate between a NextResponse 401 and a session object. Any object without .session silently passes auth. Robust approach: use instanceof NextResponse.

No CHECK constraint on score in the migration, and no validation in createMatch or the POST handler rejects negative scores. score=-999 is silently accepted. If score represents a match quality percentage (0-100), this should be enforced.

block_reasons: HIGH: Auth order inverted — feature flag runs before requireSession in all 3 API handlers
HIGH: /matches server page has zero auth/session protection — leaks all DB matches to anonymous users
HIGH: PATCH id param not validated for NaN/negative — passes unchecked values to DB layer
required_fixes_before_pass: In GET, POST (route.ts) and PATCH ([id]/route.ts): move checkAuth() call to run BEFORE isFeatureEnabled() check
In app/matches/page.tsx: add requireSession check (redirect to login if no session) and MATCHES_ENABLED guard
In [id]/route.ts after parseInt: add `if (isNaN(id) || id < 1) return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Invalid id' }, { status: 400 })`
notes: test_rewrite_count=0 confirmed, SHA checksums before/after are identical for all 5 test files. PI3 fully compliant. Migration schema correct: version=32, name=matches, IF NOT EXISTS on table and all 3 indexes, down() uses DROP IF EXISTS, all 4 status values in CHECK constraint. listMatches sortBy/sortDir are whitelisted before interpolation — no SQL injection. VALID_TRANSITIONS covers all 4 states. Error message 'Invalid transition' matches test contract.
